opportunities.title: [M02/M03] MCP proposal review, permissions and remote-agent security gates
opportunities.excerpt:
Track the follow-up engineering needed beyond the initial **synthetic local MCP** demonstration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Draft proposals cannot mutate approved family records or access private family data until M1 #9 and #10 security are complete
- [ ] User/agent identity binding, scopes, consent, approval workflow, safe audit for create/update/link actions, no self approval
- [ ] Validate prompt injection and cross-tenant enumeration; redact tool errors and prevent data exfiltration
- [ ] Per-agent capability negotiation; human approval required for publication
- [ ] Local per-user encrypted draft storage or similarly secure store with clear reset/delete; no secrets in repo
- [ ] Production HTTP MCP requires authenticated identity, exact host allowlist, Origin validation, TLS and rate limits; never expose loopback-only server externally without protection
- [ ] Investigate ChatGPT/Copilot/other agent connection capabilities at deployment time, without assuming this chat can reach localhost
- [ ] No cloud resource provisioned or paid hosting added without specific owner approval

Do not mark complete merely when read-only local tools work. Related: #9, #10, #12, #15.

opportunities.title: Claude Code hooks never see OTEL_* variables: document it and warn in doctor
opportunities.excerpt:
## Problem

Since Claude Code 2.1.128, Claude Code removes **every `OTEL_*` environment variable** from the subprocesses it spawns: the Bash tool, **hooks**, MCP servers and language servers. This is intended and documented:
- [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): "A hook process inherits the parent environment, apart from the `OTEL_*` exporter variables…"
- [monitoring page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage)
- Background: anthropics/claude-code#55105 and #45644, where Claude's OTel settings leaked into child tools.

So when otel-hook runs as a Claude Code hook, it never receives:
- the standard variables (#52, #53): `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*HEADERS`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`;
- our own `OTEL_HOOK_*` variables, which start with `OTEL_` too;
- any of these set in the `env` block of `settings.json`.

Variables without the `OTEL_` prefix are passed through unchanged. Even `OTELX_…` gets through, so the filter matches the `OTEL_` prefix exactly.

### Reproduction (Claude Code 2.1.331)

1. Add a `SessionStart` hook whose command is `env | sort > out.txt`.
2. Start `claude -p hi` with `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_HOOK_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT` and a control variable `PROBE_CONTROL` set, plus `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` in the settings `env` block.
3. `out.txt` contains only `PROBE_CONTROL` and the settings-block control variable. No `OTEL_*` variable is there.

PR #61's agent lab found the same thing.

### What still works under Claude Code

- `--config-file`, `--endpoint`, `--header` and `--resource-attr` on the hook command;
- a wrapper script that sets the variables *inside* the hook process, as HAR's `run-otel-hook.sh` does by sourcing `direct.env`.

## Work

- [ ] README: in the "Exporter headers", standard endpoint and resource-attribute sections and in the Claude Code provider notes, say that these variables do not reach Claude Code hooks, and give the supported alternatives (config file, hook-command flags, wrapper).
- [ ] `otel-hook setup --provider claude-code`: when an `OTEL_*` exporter variable is set in the shell running setup, print a hint that Claude Code hooks won't see it, and suggest `--hook-command "… --config-file …"`.
- [ ] `doctor`: when run with the Claude Code provider and the only exporter configuration comes f

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
